    17→## Items
    18→
    19→### 1. Equation (Hamiltonian)   {#eq:HN}
    20→**Kind:** equation
    21→**Tex label:** eq:HN
    22→**Depends on:** none
    23→**Statement (informal):**
    24→> The mean-field Hamiltonian for N identical unit-mass particles in ℝ^d is
    25→> H_N(X, V) = Σ_{i=1}^{N} |v_i|²/2  +  (1/N) Σ_{1 ≤ i < j ≤ N} W(x_i − x_j),
    26→> where the factor 1/N normalizes the interaction energy so that kinetic and potential energies
    27→> are of the same order as N → ∞.
    28→**Symbols introduced:**
    29→- `H_N` — the N-particle Hamiltonian; a function `(Fin N → ℝ^d) × (Fin N → ℝ^d) → ℝ`
    30→- `W` — pair potential; a function `ℝ^d → ℝ`
    31→- `N` — number of particles; `ℕ`
    32→- `d` — spatial dimension; `ℕ` with `d ≥ 1`
    33→
    34→---
    35→
    36→### 2. Equation (Hamilton / Newton equations of motion)   {#eq:newton}
    37→**Kind:** equation
    38→**Tex label:** eq:newton
    39→**Depends on:** eq:HN
    40→**Statement (informal):**
    41→> The Hamilton equations derived from H_N are
    42→> ẋ_i = v_i,   v̇_i = −(1/N) Σ_{j ≠ i} ∇W(x_i − x_j),   for i = 1, …, N.
    43→> These are the N-particle mean-field Newton equations (second-order ODE system).
    44→**Symbols introduced:**
    45→- `∇W` — gradient of the pair potential; `ℝ^d → ℝ^d`
    46→
    47→---
    48→
    49→### 3. Assumption   {#ass:W}
    50→**Kind:** assumption
    51→**Tex label:** ass:W
    52→**Depends on:** none
    53→**Statement (informal):**
    54→> The pair potential W : ℝ^d → ℝ belongs to C^{1,1}(ℝ^d) (i.e., has a globally Lipschitz
    55→> gradient), is even (W(−x) = W(x) for all x), and the Lipschitz constant of its gradient is
    56→> finite:
    57→> L := Lip(∇W) = sup_{x ≠ y} |∇W(x) − ∇W(y)| / |x − y|  <  ∞.
    58→**Symbols introduced:**
    59→- `L` — Lipschitz constant of ∇W; `ℝ≥0` (or `ℝ` with a positivity hypothesis); expected Mathlib type `NNReal` or the hypothesis `LipschitzWith L (∇W)`
    60→
    61→---
    62→
    63→### 4. Definition (Empirical measure)   {#def:empirical}
    64→**Kind:** definition
    65→**Tex label:** none
    66→**Depends on:** eq:newton
    67→**Statement (informal):**
    68→> The empirical measure of a configuration Z = (X, V) ∈ (ℝ^d × ℝ^d)^N is the probability
    69→> measure on ℝ^d × ℝ^d defined by
    70→> μ^N[Z] := (1/N) Σ_{i=1}^{N} δ_{(x_i, v_i)}.
    71→> Along a solution t ↦ (X(t), V(t)) of eq:newton, one writes μ_t^N := μ^N[X(t), V(t)].
    72→**Symbols introduced:**
    73→- `μ^N[Z]` — empirical measure; `MeasureTheory.Measure (ℝ^d × ℝ^d)`, specifically a `MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure`
    74→- `μ_t^N` — time-dependent empirical measure along a solution; a curve `ℝ → MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure (ℝ^d × ℝ^d)`
    75→- `δ_{z}` — Dirac delta at z; `MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac z`
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→### 5. Proposition (Weak evolution of the empirical measure)   {#prop:weak}
    80→**Kind:** proposition
    81→**Tex label:** prop:weak
    82→**Depends on:** eq:newton, def:empirical, ass:W
    83→**Statement (informal):**
    84→> Let (X, V) : [0, T] → (ℝ^d × ℝ^d)^N solve eq:newton, and let ρ_t^N(x) := ∫ μ_t^N(dx, dv)
    85→> be the spatial marginal. Then for every test function φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d × ℝ^d),
    86→> d/dt ⟨μ_t^N, φ⟩ = ⟨μ_t^N, v · ∇_x φ − (∇W * ρ_t^N) · ∇_v φ⟩  +  R_N(t),
    87→> where the remainder satisfies |R_N(t)| ≤ (1/N) ‖∇W‖_∞ ‖∇_v φ‖_∞ and vanishes identically
    88→> when ∇W(0) = 0. Under Assumption ass:W (W even ⟹ ∇W(0) = 0), one has R_N ≡ 0.
    89→**Symbols introduced:**
    90→- `ρ_t^N` — spatial marginal of μ_t^N; `MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ^d`
    91→- `⟨μ, φ⟩` — integral of φ against μ; `∫ φ dμ` in Mathlib notation
    92→- `∇W * ρ` — convolution of ∇W with the measure ρ; `(fun x => ∫ ∇W(x − y) dρ(y))`
    93→- `R_N(t)` — remainder term from the diagonal i = j; `ℝ`
    94→
    95→---
    96→
    97→### 6. Equation (Weak form of empirical-measure evolution)   {#eq:weak-eq}
    98→**Kind:** equation
    99→**Tex label:** eq:weak-eq
   100→**Depends on:** prop:weak
   101→**Statement (informal):**
   102→> The distributional evolution identity for the empirical measure:
   103→> d/dt ⟨μ_t^N, φ⟩  =  ⟨μ_t^N, v · ∇_x φ − (∇W * ρ_t^N) · ∇_v φ⟩  +  R_N(t),
   104→> for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d × ℝ^d), with remainder bound |R_N(t)| ≤ (1/N) ‖∇W‖_∞ ‖∇_v φ‖_∞.

   106→**Symbols introduced:**
   107→- (No new symbols beyond those in prop:weak)

   110→

   112→**Kind:** corollary
   113→**Tex label:** cor:empirical-vlasov
   114→**Depends on:** prop:weak, ass:W, eq:weak-eq, eq:vlasov
   115→**Statement (informal):**
   116→> Under Assumption ass:W, the empirical measure μ_t^N is a distributional solution of the
   117→> nonlinear Vlasov equation eq:vlasov, in the sense that eq:weak-eq holds with R_N ≡ 0 for
   118→> every φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d × ℝ^d).
   119→**Symbols introduced:**
   120→- (No new symbols)
   121→
   122→---
   123→
   124→### 8. Equation (Vlasov equation)   {#eq:vlasov}
   125→**Kind:** equation
   126→**Tex label:** eq:vlasov
   127→**Depends on:** eq:weak-eq
   128→**Statement (informal):**
   129→> The nonlinear Vlasov equation (the formal N → ∞ limit of eq:weak-eq) is the PDE
   130→> ∂_t f + v · ∇_x f − (∇W * ρ_t)(x) · ∇_v f = 0,
   131→> with ρ_t(x) = ∫_{ℝ^d} f(t, x, v) dv.
   132→> Here f = f(t, x, v) is a time-dependent probability measure on ℝ^d × ℝ^d (or a density),
   133→> and ρ_t is its spatial marginal.
   134→**Symbols introduced:**
   135→- `f` — solution of the Vlasov equation; `MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure (ℝ^d × ℝ^d)` (measure-valued), or a density `ℝ^{≥0} × ℝ^d × ℝ^d → ℝ≥0`
   136→- `ρ_t` — spatial marginal of f_t; `MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ^d`
   137→
   138→---
   139→
   140→### 9. Theorem (Existence and uniqueness for Vlasov)   {#thm:vlasov-wp}
   141→**Kind:** theorem
   142→**Tex label:** thm:vlasov-wp
   143→**Depends on:** ass:W, eq:vlasov, eq:char
   144→**Statement (informal):**
   145→> Let f_0 ∈ 𝒫_1(ℝ^d × ℝ^d) be a probability measure with finite first moment. Under
   146→> Assumption ass:W, there exists a unique narrowly continuous curve t ↦ f_t ∈ 𝒫_1(ℝ^d × ℝ^d)
   147→> satisfying the Vlasov equation eq:vlasov in the distributional sense with initial condition
   148→> f_{t=0} = f_0.
   149→**Symbols introduced:**
   150→- `𝒫_1(ℝ^d × ℝ^d)` — probability measures on ℝ^d × ℝ^d with finite first moment; `MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure` with an additional `∫ ‖z‖ dμ < ∞` hypothesis (Mathlib: `MeasureTheory.Memℒp` or `HasFiniteIntegral`)
   151→
   152→---
   153→
   154→### 10. Equation (Characteristic / mean-field ODE)   {#eq:char}
   155→**Kind:** equation
   156→**Tex label:** eq:char
   157→**Depends on:** eq:vlasov
   158→**Statement (informal):**
   159→> The mean-field characteristic ODE associated to the Vlasov equation is
   160→> Ẋ(t, z) = V(t, z),   V̇(t, z) = −(∇W * ρ_t)(X(t, z)),   (X, V)(0, z) = z,
   161→> where ρ_t = (X(t, ·))_# (∫ f_0 dv) is the pushforward of the initial spatial marginal
   162→> under the position flow. The solution f_t is then the pushforward f_t = (X(t,·), V(t,·))_# f_0.
   163→**Symbols introduced:**
   164→- `X(t, z)` — position component of the characteristic flow; `ℝ → ℝ^d × ℝ^d → ℝ^d`
   165→- `V(t, z)` — velocity component of the characteristic flow; `ℝ → ℝ^d × ℝ^d → ℝ^d`
   166→- `(Φ)_# μ` — pushforward of a measure under a map Φ; `MeasureTheory.Measure.map`
   167→
   168→---
   169→
   170→### 11. Theorem (Dobrushin, 1979)   {#thm:dobrushin}
   171→**Kind:** theorem
   172→**Tex label:** thm:dobrushin
   173→**Depends on:** ass:W, eq:vlasov, eq:dobrushin
   174→**Statement (informal):**
   175→> Under Assumption ass:W, there exists a constant C = C(L) > 0 such that for any two
   176→> measure-valued solutions f_t, g_t ∈ 𝒫_1(ℝ^d × ℝ^d) of the Vlasov equation eq:vlasov,

   178→> where W_1 is the Wasserstein-1 distance. The proof (sketched in the paper) uses a coupling
   179→> argument via the characteristic flows eq:char and a Gronwall inequality; the key estimate is
   180→> |∇W * ρ − ∇W * σ|_∞ ≤ L · W_1(ρ, σ). Attribution: Dobrushin (1979), see [Dobrushin].
   181→**Symbols introduced:**
   182→- `W_1(μ, ν)` — Wasserstein-1 (Kantorovich–Rubinstein) distance; `MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.wasserstein 1` or `MeasureTheory.Measure.toFiniteWasserstein` in Mathlib
   183→- `C(L)` — explicit constant depending only on L = Lip(∇W); `ℝ`, stated to exist but not given explicitly
   184→
   185→---
   186→
   187→### 12. Equation (Dobrushin stability estimate)   {#eq:dobrushin}
   188→**Kind:** equation
   189→**Tex label:** eq:dobrushin
   190→**Depends on:** thm:dobrushin
   191→**Statement (informal):**
   192→> The exponential Wasserstein-1 stability estimate for Vlasov solutions:
   193→> W_1(f_t, g_t) ≤ e^{Ct} · W_1(f_0, g_0),   for all t ≥ 0,
   194→> for any two measure solutions f_t, g_t of eq:vlasov. This is the content of Theorem thm:dobrushin.
   195→**Symbols introduced:**
   196→- (No new symbols beyond those in thm:dobrushin)
   197→
   198→---
   199→

   201→**Kind:** corollary
   202→**Tex label:** cor:mfl
   203→**Depends on:** thm:dobrushin, cor:empirical-vlasov, eq:dobrushin
   204→**Statement (informal):**
   205→> Let f_0 ∈ 𝒫_1(ℝ^d × ℝ^d), and let (X_0^N, V_0^N) be initial particle data whose empirical
   206→> measure μ_0^N satisfies W_1(μ_0^N, f_0) → 0 as N → ∞. Under Assumption ass:W, for every

   208→> sup_{t ∈ [0,T]} W_1(μ_t^N, f_t) ≤ e^{CT} · W_1(μ_0^N, f_0)  →  0   as N → ∞,

   210→> is the empirical measure of the N-particle system. This is the mean-field limit theorem.

    24→abbrev PhysSpace (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

    30→-- §1  Equation (Hamiltonian)   (tex: eq:HN)

    33→/-- (tex: eq:HN)
    34→The mean-field Hamiltonian for N identical unit-mass particles in ℝ^d:
    35→
    36→  H_N(X, V) = Σ_{i=1}^{N} |v_i|² / 2  +  (1/N) Σ_{1 ≤ i < j ≤ N} W(x_i − x_j).
    37→

    39→energies are of the same order as N → ∞.
    40→-/
    41→noncomputable def hamiltonianN (N : ℕ) (W : PhysSpace d → ℝ)
    42→    (X V : Fin N → PhysSpace d) : ℝ :=
    43→  (∑ i : Fin N, ‖V i‖ ^ 2 / 2)
    44→  + (1 / (N : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin N, ∑ j : Fin N,
    45→      if (i : ℕ) < j then W (X i - X j) else 0
    46→
    47→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    48→-- §2  Equation (Hamilton / Newton equations of motion)   (tex: eq:newton)
    49→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    50→
    51→/-- (tex: eq:newton)
    52→Predicate asserting that a curve (X, V) : ℝ → (Fin N → PhysSpace d)²
    53→satisfies the N-particle mean-field Newton equations
    54→
    55→  ẋ_i = v_i,
    56→  v̇_i = −(1/N) Σ_{j ≠ i} ∇W(x_i − x_j),   i = 1, …, N.
    57→
    58→`gradW` is the gradient ∇W : ℝ^d → ℝ^d of the pair potential.
    59→-/
    60→def IsNewtonSolution (N : ℕ) (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
    61→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d) : Prop :=
    62→  -- position equations: Ẋ_i(t) = V_i(t)
    63→  (∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun t => X t i) (V t i) t) ∧
    64→  -- velocity equations: V̇_i(t) = −(1/N) Σ_{j ≠ i} ∇W(X_i(t) − X_j(t))
    65→  (∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun t => V t i)
    66→      (-(1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, if j ≠ i then gradW (X t i - X t j) else 0)
    67→      t)
    68→
    69→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    70→-- §3  Assumption   (tex: ass:W)
    71→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    72→
    73→/-- (tex: ass:W)
    74→Standing assumption on the pair potential W : ℝ^d → ℝ.
    75→
    76→W belongs to C^{1,1}(ℝ^d): it is differentiable with a globally Lipschitz
    77→gradient.  Additionally W is even: W(−x) = W(x) for all x.
    78→The Lipschitz constant L := Lip(∇W) is finite.
    79→-/
    80→class AssW (W : PhysSpace d → ℝ) : Prop where
    81→  /-- W is continuously differentiable. -/
    82→  differentiable : Differentiable ℝ W
    83→  /-- W is even. -/
    84→  even : ∀ x : PhysSpace d, W (-x) = W x
    85→  /-- The gradient ∇W is Lipschitz with some constant L ≥ 0. -/
    86→  lipschitzGrad : ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (fun x => fderiv ℝ W x)
    87→
    88→omit [NeZero d] in
    89→/-- Helper: under `[AssW W]` (even + differentiable), the gradient of `W`
    90→at the origin vanishes.
    91→
    92→Mathematical content: differentiating `W(-x) = W(x)` at `x = 0` and using
    93→`HasFDerivAt.unique` gives `fderiv W 0 = -fderiv W 0`, hence
    94→`gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0`. In the real vector space `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`
    95→this forces `gradient W 0 = 0`.
    96→
    97→Used by `empiricalMeasureSolvesVlasov` (cor:empirical-vlasov) to kill the
    98→diagonal correction term in `weakEvolutionEmpiricalMeasure`. -/
    99→lemma gradient_zero_of_even (W : PhysSpace d → ℝ) [hW : AssW W] :
   100→    gradient W 0 = 0 := by
   101→  -- Step A: the claim that the gradient at 0 equals its own negation.
   102→  suffices h : gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0 by
   103→    -- x = -x in a ℝ-vector space ⟹ x = 0.
   104→    have h2 : gradient W 0 + gradient W 0 = 0 := by
   105→      nth_rewrite 2 [h]
   106→      exact add_neg_cancel (gradient W 0)
   107→    -- Rewrite x + x as 2 • x and use the real-vector-space cancellation.
   108→    have h3 : (2 : ℝ) • gradient W 0 = 0 := by
   109→      rw [show (2 : ℝ) • gradient W 0 = gradient W 0 + gradient W 0 from by
   110→            rw [two_smul]]
   111→      exact h2
   112→    exact (smul_eq_zero.mp h3).resolve_left (by norm_num)
   113→  -- Step B: prove gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0 via the fderiv chain rule on
   114→  -- the (trivial) composition W ∘ Neg.neg = W.
   115→  have hdiff : Differentiable ℝ W := hW.differentiable
   116→  -- Strategy: prove `gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0` by exhibiting two
   117→  -- HasFDerivAt witnesses for W at 0 and invoking uniqueness.
   118→  -- The first witness is the standard `fderiv ℝ W 0`; the second comes
   119→  -- from the chain rule on `(fun x => W (-x))`, which equals W by
   120→  -- evenness.
   121→  have h_W0 : HasFDerivAt W (fderiv ℝ W 0) 0 :=
   122→    hdiff.differentiableAt.hasFDerivAt
   123→  -- Derivative of `(fun x : PhysSpace d => -x)` at 0 is `-id` (as a CLM).
   124→  -- We get it from `hasFDerivAt_id` and `.neg` (which negates the function
   125→  -- pointwise, equivalent to applying negation to the argument).
   126→  have h_neg : HasFDerivAt (fun x : PhysSpace d => -x)
   127→      (-ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (PhysSpace d)) 0 :=
   128→    (hasFDerivAt_id (𝕜 := ℝ) (0 : PhysSpace d)).neg
   129→  -- Need h_W0 phrased at `-(0 : PhysSpace d)` for the chain rule below.
   130→  have h_W_at_neg0 : HasFDerivAt W (fderiv ℝ W 0) (-(0 : PhysSpace d)) := by
   131→    rw [neg_zero]; exact h_W0
   132→  -- Chain rule applied to W ∘ (-·) gives `HasFDerivAt (fun x => W (-x)) ...`.
   133→  have h_chain : HasFDerivAt (fun x : PhysSpace d => W (-x))
   134→      ((fderiv ℝ W 0).comp (-ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (PhysSpace d))) 0 :=
   135→    h_W_at_neg0.comp 0 h_neg
   136→  -- Evenness rewrites `(fun x => W (-x))` to `W`, giving a second
   137→  -- HasFDerivAt witness for W at 0.
   138→  have hcomp_eq : (fun x : PhysSpace d => W (-x)) = W := funext hW.even
   139→  rw [hcomp_eq] at h_chain
   140→  -- Uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative.
   141→  have h_fderiv : fderiv ℝ W 0
   142→      = (fderiv ℝ W 0).comp (-ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (PhysSpace d)) :=
   143→    h_W0.unique h_chain
   144→  -- f.comp (-id) = -f for any CLM f.
   145→  have h_comp_neg : (fderiv ℝ W 0).comp (-ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (PhysSpace d))
   146→      = -(fderiv ℝ W 0) := by
   147→    ext v
   148→    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.neg_apply,
   149→               ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.map_neg]
   150→  rw [h_comp_neg] at h_fderiv
   151→  -- Push `fderiv ℝ W 0 = -fderiv ℝ W 0` through `(toDual).symm`
   152→  -- (a linear isomorphism) to land at `gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0`.
   153→  have h_grad : gradient W 0 = -gradient W 0 :=
   154→    (congrArg (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (PhysSpace d)).symm h_fderiv).trans
   155→      (map_neg _ _)
   156→  exact h_grad
   157→

   159→-- §4  Definition (Empirical measure)   (tex: def:empirical)
   160→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   161→
   162→-- TODO(mathlib): Mathlib does not yet have a ready-made `empiricalMeasure`
   163→-- construction returning a `ProbabilityMeasure`.  We define it here as a
   164→-- placeholder using `MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac` and a finite sum.
   165→
   166→/-- (tex: def:empirical)
   167→The empirical measure of a configuration (X, V) ∈ (ℝ^d × ℝ^d)^N:
   168→
   169→  μ^N[X, V] := (1/N) Σ_{i=1}^{N} δ_{(X_i, V_i)}.
   170→
   171→Returns a `MeasureTheory.Measure (PhaseSpace d)`.  It is a probability measure
   172→when N ≥ 1.
   173→-/
   174→noncomputable def empiricalMeasure (N : ℕ) (X V : Fin N → PhysSpace d) :
   175→    Measure (PhaseSpace d) :=
   176→  (1 / (N : ENNReal)) • ∑ i : Fin N, Measure.dirac (X i, V i)
   177→
   178→omit [NeZero d] in
   179→/-- (tex: def:empirical)
   180→When N ≥ 1 the empirical measure is a probability measure.
   181→
   182→Proof: μ(univ) = (1/N) · Σᵢ δ_{zᵢ}(univ) = (1/N) · N · 1 = 1, where each
   183→Dirac mass evaluates to 1 on the universal set via the
   184→`Measure.dirac.isProbabilityMeasure` instance. -/
   185→lemma empiricalMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   186→    (X V : Fin N → PhysSpace d) :
   187→    IsProbabilityMeasure (empiricalMeasure N X V) := by
   188→  refine ⟨?_⟩
   189→  simp only [empiricalMeasure, Measure.smul_apply, Measure.finset_sum_apply,
   190→             measure_univ, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin,
   191→             smul_eq_mul, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   192→  exact ENNReal.div_mul_cancel
   193→    (Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (NeZero.ne N)) (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top N)
   194→
   195→/-- (tex: def:empirical)
   196→The time-dependent empirical measure μ_t^N along a solution of eq:newton. -/
   197→noncomputable def empiricalMeasureCurve (N : ℕ) (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d) :
   198→    ℝ → Measure (PhaseSpace d) :=
   199→  fun t => empiricalMeasure N (X t) (V t)

   202→-- §5  Proposition (Weak evolution of the empirical measure)   (tex: prop:weak)
   203→-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   204→
   205→-- TODO(mathlib): Convolution of a function with a measure (∇W * ρ) is used
   206→-- below.  In Mathlib this would be `MeasureTheory.Measure.convolution` or a
   207→-- hand-rolled integral.  We give a local definition as a placeholder.
   208→
   209→/-- Convolution of a function k : ℝ^d → ℝ^d with a (finite) measure ρ on ℝ^d:
   210→  (k * ρ)(x) := ∫ k(x − y) dρ(y).
   211→-/
   212→noncomputable def convolveFunctionMeasure (k : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   213→    (ρ : Measure (PhysSpace d)) (x : PhysSpace d) : PhysSpace d :=
   214→  ∫ y, k (x - y) ∂ρ

   216→/-- Spatial marginal of a measure on phase space. -/
   217→noncomputable def spatialMarginal (μ : Measure (PhaseSpace d)) :
   218→    Measure (PhysSpace d) :=
   219→  Measure.map Prod.fst μ
   220→
   221→/-! Decomposed by sorry-decomposer.
   222→    See `formalize/plans/weakEvolutionEmpiricalMeasure.json`. -/
   223→
   224→/-- The integral of a function φ against the empirical measure `empiricalMeasure N X V`
   225→equals `(1/N) * ∑ i, φ(X i, V i)`, by unfolding the weighted sum of Dirac masses. -/
   226→lemma empiricalMeasure_integral_eq (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   227→    (X V : Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   228→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ) :
   229→    ∫ z, φ z ∂(empiricalMeasure N X V) =
   230→      (1 / (N : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin N, φ (X i, V i) := by
   231→  simp only [empiricalMeasure]
   232→  rw [integral_smul_measure]
   233→  rw [integral_finset_sum_measure (fun i _ => integrable_dirac (by simp))]
   234→  simp [integral_dirac, ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_natCast, smul_eq_mul]
   235→
   236→/-- For a smooth test function φ, the chain rule gives: the map `t ↦ φ(X t i, V t i)` has
   237→derivative `⟨V t i, gradXφ (X t i, V t i)⟩ + ⟨a t i, gradVφ (X t i, V t i)⟩` at t,
   238→where `a t i` is the acceleration vector at particle i and time t.
   239→
   240→Signature refactored (Phase B of the 2026-05-25 plan): φ's Fréchet derivative is
   241→an INPUT hypothesis `hφ_fderiv` instead of being derived inside the helper.  This
   242→lifts the `ContDiff.hasFDerivAt + WithLp.toLp + gradient → toDual → toLinearMap`
   243→type-class friction up to the call site (where `ContDiff ℝ ⊤ φ` is already a
   244→hypothesis and the Fréchet derivative is a one-line `have`).  The body of this
   245→helper is then a straight composition:
   246→  · `HasDerivAt.prodMk hX hV` gives the curve derivative `t ↦ (X t i, V t i)`.
   247→  · `(hφ_fderiv (X t i, V t i)).comp_hasDerivAt` composes through φ.
   248→  · Unfolding `gradXφ`/`gradVφ` via `hgradXφ`/`hgradVφ` and rewriting the
   249→    Fréchet derivative's action via `inner_product` partial-derivative
   250→    identities gives the target inner-product form. -/
   251→lemma hasDerivAt_phi_along_trajectory (N : ℕ)
   252→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   253→    (hX : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun t => X t i) (V t i) t)
   254→    (a : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   255→    (hV : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun t => V t i) (a t i) t)
   256→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ)
   257→    (φ' : PhaseSpace d → (PhaseSpace d →L[ℝ] ℝ))
   258→    (hφ_fderiv : ∀ z, HasFDerivAt φ (φ' z) z)
   259→    (gradXφ gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   260→    (hgradXφ : ∀ z, gradXφ z = gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1)
   261→    (hgradVφ : ∀ z, gradVφ z = gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2)
   262→    (t : ℝ) (i : Fin N) :
   263→    HasDerivAt (fun s => φ (X s i, V s i))
   264→      (@inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (V t i) (gradXφ (X t i, V t i)) +
   265→       @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (a t i) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))) t := by
   266→  -- Step 1: curve derivative
   267→  have hcurve : HasDerivAt (fun s => (X s i, V s i)) (V t i, a t i) t :=
   268→    (hX t i).prodMk (hV t i)
   269→  -- Step 2: compose φ through the curve
   270→  have hcomp : HasDerivAt (fun s => φ (X s i, V s i))
   271→      ((φ' (X t i, V t i)) (V t i, a t i)) t :=
   272→    (hφ_fderiv (X t i, V t i)).comp_hasDerivAt t hcurve
   273→  -- Step 3: rewrite the derivative value
   274→  convert hcomp using 1
   275→  -- Step 4: show φ'(z)(V,a) = ⟨V, gradXφ z⟩ + ⟨a, gradVφ z⟩
   276→  set z := (X t i, V t i)
   277→  -- partial x: HasFDerivAt (fun x => φ(x, z.2)) (φ' z ∘L inl ℝ _ _) z.1
   278→  have hpX : HasFDerivAt (fun x => φ (x, z.2))
   279→      ((φ' z).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inl ℝ (PhysSpace d) (PhysSpace d))) z.1 :=
   280→    (hφ_fderiv z).comp z.1 (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_left z.1 z.2)
   281→  have hpV : HasFDerivAt (fun v => φ (z.1, v))
   282→      ((φ' z).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ (PhysSpace d) (PhysSpace d))) z.2 :=
   283→    (hφ_fderiv z).comp z.2 (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_right z.1 z.2)
   284→  simp only [hgradXφ z, hgradVφ z]
   285→  -- inner(V, ∇f z.1) = fderiv f z.1 V via inner_gradient_right (real case: conj = id)
   286→  have hgX : @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (V t i) (gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1) =
   287→      fderiv ℝ (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1 (V t i) := by
   288→    rw [inner_gradient_right hpX.differentiableAt]
   289→    simp [RCLike.conj_eq_iff_re, conj_trivial]
   290→  have hgV : @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (a t i) (gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2) =
   291→      fderiv ℝ (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2 (a t i) := by
   292→    rw [inner_gradient_right hpV.differentiableAt]
   293→    simp [RCLike.conj_eq_iff_re, conj_trivial]
   294→  rw [hgX, hgV, hpX.fderiv, hpV.fderiv]
   295→  simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.inl_apply,
   296→        ContinuousLinearMap.inr_apply]
   297→  rw [← map_add]
   298→  simp [Prod.mk_add_mk]
   299→
   300→/-- The derivative of `t ↦ ∫ φ d(empiricalMeasureCurve N X V t)` equals the finite sum
   301→expression `(1/N) * Σᵢ [⟨V t i, gradXφ (X t i, V t i)⟩ + ⟨aᵢ, gradVφ (X t i, V t i)⟩]`
   302→where `aᵢ = -(1/N) Σ_{j≠i} gradW(X t i - X t j)` is the Newton acceleration,
   303→obtained by combining `empiricalMeasure_integral_eq` and `hasDerivAt_phi_along_trajectory`
   304→with `HasDerivAt.sum` and `HasDerivAt.const_smul`. -/
   305→lemma hasDerivAt_empiricalIntegral_sum (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   306→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   307→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   308→    (hSol : IsNewtonSolution N gradW X V)
   309→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ)
   310→    (hφ_smooth : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ φ)
   311→    (gradXφ gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   312→    (hgradXφ : ∀ z, gradXφ z = gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1)
   313→    (hgradVφ : ∀ z, gradVφ z = gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2)
   314→    (t : ℝ) :
   315→    HasDerivAt (fun s => ∫ z, φ z ∂(empiricalMeasureCurve N X V s))
   316→      ((1 / (N : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin N,
   317→        (@inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (V t i) (gradXφ (X t i, V t i)) +
   318→         @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (
   319→           -(1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, if j ≠ i then gradW (X t i - X t j) else 0)
   320→           (gradVφ (X t i, V t i)))) t := by
   321→  -- Construct φ's Fréchet derivative witness from smoothness.
   322→  have hφ_diff : Differentiable ℝ φ := hφ_smooth.differentiable (by norm_num)
   323→  have hφ_fderiv : ∀ z, HasFDerivAt φ (fderiv ℝ φ z) z := fun z =>
   324→    hφ_diff.differentiableAt.hasFDerivAt
   325→  -- The Newton-acceleration function, packaged for hasDerivAt_phi_along_trajectory.
   326→  let acc : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d := fun s i =>
   327→    -(1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, if j ≠ i then gradW (X s i - X s j) else 0
   328→  -- Rewrite the integral via empiricalMeasure_integral_eq (per-time-slice).
   329→  have hint : ∀ s : ℝ, ∫ z, φ z ∂(empiricalMeasureCurve N X V s) =
   330→      (1 / (N : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin N, φ (X s i, V s i) := fun s => by
   331→    simp only [empiricalMeasureCurve]
   332→    exact empiricalMeasure_integral_eq N (X s) (V s) φ
   333→  simp_rw [hint]
   334→  -- Differentiate (1/N) * Σᵢ φ(Xₛᵢ, Vₛᵢ) wrt s.  Establish the per-particle
   335→  -- derivative via hasDerivAt_phi_along_trajectory (using `acc` for the
   336→  -- Newton acceleration), combine termwise via HasDerivAt.sum, then pull
   337→  -- the (1/N) constant out via HasDerivAt.const_mul.
   338→  have h_each : ∀ i : Fin N,
   339→      HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => φ (X s i, V s i))
   340→        (@inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (V t i) (gradXφ (X t i, V t i)) +
   341→         @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (acc t i) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i))) t := fun i =>
   342→    hasDerivAt_phi_along_trajectory N X V hSol.1 acc hSol.2 φ
   343→      (fderiv ℝ φ) hφ_fderiv gradXφ gradVφ hgradXφ hgradVφ t i
   344→  have h_sum : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => ∑ i : Fin N, φ (X s i, V s i))
   345→      (∑ i : Fin N,
   346→        (@inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (V t i) (gradXφ (X t i, V t i)) +
   347→         @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _ (acc t i) (gradVφ (X t i, V t i)))) t :=
   348→    HasDerivAt.fun_sum (fun i _ => h_each i)
   349→  exact h_sum.const_mul (1 / (N : ℝ))
   350→
   351→/-- Convolution of the kernel `gradW` against the spatial marginal of the
   352→empirical measure unfolds to the explicit finite sum
   353→`(1/N) • Σⱼ gradW(X t i − X t j)`.  This is the API-navigation step that
   354→separates the Measure-pushforward / Dirac-integration machinery from the
   355→algebraic "add and subtract the diagonal" step in `diagonalCorrection_eq`.
   356→
   357→Proof strategy (decomposer-supplied mathlib_hints, grep-validated against
   358→Mathlib 4.x at `.lake/packages/mathlib/`):
   359→  1. `empiricalMeasureCurve` and `empiricalMeasure` unfold to
   360→     `(1/N : ℝ≥0∞) • Σⱼ Measure.dirac (X t j, V t j)`.
   361→  2. `Measure.map_smul` (`MeasureTheory/Measure/Map.lean:127`) pushes
   362→     `Prod.fst` through the scalar.
   363→  3. `Measure.map_add` (`MeasureTheory/Measure/Map.lean:103`) + finset
   364→     induction distributes `Prod.fst` over the sum, giving
   365→     `(1/N : ℝ≥0∞) • Σⱼ Measure.dirac (X t j)`.
   366→  4. `convolveFunctionMeasure` unfolds to `∫ y, gradW(X t i − y) ∂ρ`.
   367→  5. `integral_smul_measure` (Bochner) extracts the `(1/N).toReal = 1/N`
   368→     scalar; `integral_finset_sum_measure` (`Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean:1018`)
   369→     distributes integration over the finite sum of Diracs;
   370→     `integral_dirac'` (`Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean:1131`) collapses each
   371→     summand to `gradW(X t i − X t j)`. -/
   372→lemma convolveFunctionMeasure_empiricalSpatial_eq (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   373→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   374→    (hgradW_meas : Measurable gradW)
   375→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d) (t : ℝ) (i : Fin N) :
   376→    convolveFunctionMeasure gradW
   377→        (spatialMarginal (empiricalMeasureCurve N X V t)) (X t i) =
   378→      (1 / (N : ℝ)) • ∑ j : Fin N, gradW (X t i - X t j) := by
   379→  -- Measurability witnesses
   380→  have hmeas_y : Measurable (fun y : PhysSpace d => gradW (X t i - y)) :=
   381→    hgradW_meas.comp (measurable_const.sub measurable_id)
   382→  have hsm_y : StronglyMeasurable (fun y : PhysSpace d => gradW (X t i - y)) :=
   383→    hmeas_y.stronglyMeasurable
   384→  have hmeas_z : Measurable (fun z : PhaseSpace d => gradW (X t i - z.1)) :=
   385→    hgradW_meas.comp (measurable_const.sub measurable_fst)

   543→

   560→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   561→    (hgradW : ∀ x, gradW x = gradient W x)
   562→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
   563→    (hSol : IsNewtonSolution N gradW X V)
   564→    -- φ is a smooth compactly supported test function on phase space
   565→    (φ : PhaseSpace d → ℝ)
   566→    (hφ_smooth : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ φ)
   567→    (hφ_compact : HasCompactSupport φ)
   568→    -- ∇_x φ and ∇_v φ regarded as functions
   569→    (gradXφ gradVφ : PhaseSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   570→    (hgradXφ : ∀ z, gradXφ z = gradient (fun x => φ (x, z.2)) z.1)
   571→    (hgradVφ : ∀ z, gradVφ z = gradient (fun v => φ (z.1, v)) z.2)

   574→    -- the RHS collapse to junk value 0 on `ℝ`, making the bound vacuous

   585→    -- contributes `gradW 0`).

   587→      -- explicit formula for the remainder

   637→                  @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _
   638→                    (convolveFunctionMeasure gradW

   682→              @inner ℝ (PhysSpace d) _
   683→                (convolveFunctionMeasure gradW (spatialMarginal (μ t)) z.1)
   684→                (gradVφ z))

   699→    (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
   700→    (W : PhysSpace d → ℝ) [hW : AssW W]
   701→    (gradW : PhysSpace d → PhysSpace d)
   702→    (hgradW : ∀ x, gradW x = gradient W x)
   703→    (X V : ℝ → Fin N → PhysSpace d)
